issues.description: PR description says CloseStream but code sends type Close — the control message string is unverified against Deepgram's actual API.
issues.detail: The PR rationale references {"type": "CloseStream"} (per Deepgram's Listen V1), but _CLOSE_MSG is {"type": "Close"}. Speak V1 may indeed use Close, but the discrepancy in the PR description means the invariant the fix depends on — that this exact string causes graceful drain — is unaudited. State which message the Speak socket actually accepts and cite it.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout does not establish the invariant that all pending audio has been drained.
issues.detail: The stated goal is to wait for the server to flush remaining audio/transcripts before close. But receive() returns on the first frame — which may be a single audio chunk, a ping, or a control ack — not on end-of-stream. Either loop until a Close/Closed frame (or until timeout), or document explicitly that this is a best-effort grace period, not a drain.

issues.description: Bare Exception catch around send_str swallows cancellation and obscures the actual failure mode.
issues.detail: except Exception will catch programming errors (e.g., ws already closed, JSON encoding bugs that won't happen here, type errors) and downgrade them to a warning. Narrow to ConnectionResetError / aiohttp.ClientError / asyncio.TimeoutError. Also: log at debug if the socket is already closed — that is the expected race, not a warning.

issues.description: Constants are class attributes built at import time via json.dumps — fine, but the literate comment is missing.
issues.detail: _FLUSH_MSG and _CLOSE_MSG are protocol-level control frames whose exact wire format is load-bearing. A one-line comment citing the Deepgram Speak V1 message spec (URL + which message type drains vs terminates) would make the code readable to the next maintainer without a git-blame archaeology trip. This is the literate-comment the fix needs.

issues.description: 1.0s constant timeout is a magic number with no justification or measurement behind it.
issues.detail: The PR claims this prevents 429s from lingering sessions, but 1.0s is unmeasured — could be too short under network jitter (defeating the fix) or too long for hot paths (latency tax on every close). Either cite the measurement that produced 1.0s, make it a named constant with rationale, or expose it as configurable. Don't optimize what you didn't measure.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The fix is directionally correct — sending a drain/close control message before WebSocket close mirrors the STT path and aligns with Deepgram's documented behavior — but the rigor is missing. The exact control-message string disagrees with the PR description (Close vs CloseStream), the 1-second wait is a single receive() rather than a drain loop, and the 1.0s timeout is an unmeasured magic number. Add a literate comment citing the Speak V1 spec, narrow the exception handler, and either prove or document that one receive() is sufficient. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.
